newsitem.title: FINLAND: LANNEN SEES FIM 1 BLN SALES BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: LANNEN SEES FIM 1 BLN SALES BY 2000.

text.p: Finnish food industry group Lannen Tehtaat Oy said on Tuesday it aimed by the year 2000 for annual net sales of one billion markka, a return on investment of 13 percent and to keep the equity ratio at no less than 50 percent.
"Today it looks like we will achieve our goals already before 2000," chief executive Olli Karkkila told the annual general meeting according to a company statement.
Lannen repeated an earlier forecast that 1997 net sales would rise above 900 million markka and of earnings slightly better than in 1996.
On March 3, Lannen reported 1996 profit before extraordinary items down to 48.5 million markka from 50.0 million in 1995 and net sales up to 866.6 million markka from 783.1 million.

"So far competition from imports has had a minor effect on Lannen Tehtaat's food industry business, but at the end of 1996 and in the past few months, there have been signs of big international corporations becoming more active in the Finnish market," Lannen said in the statement.
Foodstuffs now accounted for two-thirds of Lannen's net sales, and the main growth area was frozen foods, it said.
